# Written by plan_game_fanorona/twin/fanorona.py, a second implementation in
# Python made from the rules text alone. Do not edit: regenerate. One row a
# position: the position, a tab, its WHOLE MOVES sorted. A whole move is a
# paika, or a chain of steps by one stone that each take; the mover may stop
# after any step, so every beginning of a chain is a row entry of its own.
#
# The first 45 rows are every node to depth 2 from the set-up. Then random
# positions of 2 to 44 stones, and "thickets" of one to three stones among
# many enemies, which is where long chains live. Rows longer than 2,000
# characters were left out to keep the file small; the full set, 3,000
# positions, is compared by plan_game_fanorona/twin/compare.sh.
